Order 
This is first criminal appeal filed by the appellant under Section 14-A of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act in connection with FIR/Crime No.148/2025 registered at Police Station Biaora City,
District Rajgarh for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 450 of IPC, 1860 and Sections 3(1)(w)(i), 3(2)(v- a) and 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
2. Prosecution story in brief is that the appellant was working as recovery agent of a financial institution and he met the prosecutrix in connection with official work in the year 2023.

When no one was present in the house of the prosecutrix, he committed rape with her on 01.03.2023 and thereafter he created pressure upon the prosecutrix to continue in relationship, so also threatened her.
Several times he committed rape and when this matter came to the knowledge of the husband of the prosecutrix, the present FIR was lodged.
Appellant is in custody since 13.04.2025.
3. Learned counsel for appellant submits that the appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case due to some other disputes.
He further NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:14053 2 CRA-4678-2025 submits that there was inordinate delay in lodging the FIR.
He further submits that appellant is in custody since 13.04.2025, the investigation is almost over therefore, the appellant be enlarged on bail.

4. Learned Government Advocate appearing on behalf of State opposed the appeal on the ground that the prosecutrix has supported the prosecution case in her statement recorded under Section 183 of BNSS, 2023 and she has not been examined during trial till now.
He submitted that prima-facie sufficient evidence is available against the appellant.
He prays for dismissal of appeal.
